claims.head: Unstoppable force vs. Immovable object
claims.body: The Red Wings are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Panthers are the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Red Wings’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. The Panthers take a lot of penalties and the Red Wings draw plenty of them, so their power play should get its chances.

story.head: DeBrincat’s favorite opponent
paras: The Red Wings already played in Florida once this season and left with a 5-3 win on Nov 2. The Red Wings (7-7-3) lost 2-1 to Vegas on Nov 5, while the Panthers (9-5-2) beat Chicago 5-3 on Nov 4. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Wings last (20th in the NHL) and the Panthers fifth (tied for 11th). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Red Wings have played better than their record (.500) says: their chances are worth about .597, and their finishing has held them back. The Panthers’ record (.625) is about what their chances are worth.

The Red Wings block more shots than almost anyone (2nd), leave the shooting to their forwards (3rd lowest) and draw more penalties than they take (3rd). As for the Panthers, they forecheck harder than anyone (1st) and hit a lot (1st). They also have the league’s best penalty kill (1st), and the Red Wings’ power play against their penalty killers is strength against strength. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Alex DeBrincat (7 G / 9 A / 16 P in 17 GP) leads the Red Wings in scoring, with a point in eight straight games against Florida. Viktor Arvidsson (8 G / 7 A / 15 P in 17 GP) has a team-high eight goals. For the Panthers, Matthew Tkachuk (4 G / 18 A / 22 P in 16 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Sam Reinhart (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 16 GP) has a team-high nine goals, with eight points in his last five games.

Daniil Tarasov (2-2-2 / .930 SV% in 5 GS) has been a rock in net for Detroit and will likely start. Florida has two options in net: Akira Schmid (5-2-1 / .888 SV% in 7 GS) and Jacob Markström (4-2-1 / .885 SV% in 8 GS). Schmid has started six of their last ten games, so expect him back in net after Markström got the last one on Nov 4. Markström has a .855 save percentage in six starts against the Red Wings, well under his usual .898. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
At home, Paul Maurice likes to send Luostarinen, Lundell and Eller out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against DeBrincat, Finnie and Arvidsson.
